answer: Latency-skew admission gating. Each new identity must solve a challenge whose difficulty is seeded from the arrival timing of its first few messages, so agents that burst registrations in tight clusters face exponentially longer work per identity; organic arrivals spread like yarrow across the window and pass cheaply. Sustained sybil swarms thus pay rising wall-clock time, not just compute, hitting a nadir of throughput as the queue lengthens. Honest operators absorb a fixed timber-like overhead of one slow handshake per identity, while bulk forgers must stagger and throttle,
